verses.text: After this, David asked the LORD, "Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?" The LORD said, "Go up." David asked, "Where should I go?" The LORD said, "To Hebron."
So David went up there with his two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
David also brought the men who were with him, each with his family, and they lived in the towns around Hebron.
Then the men of Judah came and anointed David as king over the people of Judah. They told David, "The men of Jabesh Gilead are the ones who buried Saul."
So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh Gilead to say to them, "May the LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to your master Saul by burying him.
Now may the LORD show you his faithful love and truth. I will also be good to you because you have done this.
So now be strong and brave. Your master Saul is dead, and the people of Judah have anointed me as their king."
But Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Ishbosheth, Saul's son, across to Mahanaim.
There he made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and all Israel.
Ishbosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he ruled for two years. But the people of Judah followed David.
David was king in Hebron over the people of Judah for seven years and six months.
Abner son of Ner, with the servants of Ishbosheth son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
Joab son of Zeruiah and David's servants also went out and met them at the pool of Gibeon. One group sat down on one side of the pool, and the other group on the other side.
Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men get up and fight in front of us!" Joab said, "Let them get up."
So they got up and were counted off: twelve for Benjamin and Ishbosheth son of Saul, and twelve of David's servants.
Each man grabbed his opponent by the head and pushed his sword into the other man's side, and they all fell down together. So that place in Gibeon was called Helkath Hazzurim.
The battle that day was very fierce, and Abner and the men of Israel were beaten by David's servants.
The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a wild gazelle.
Asahel chased Abner, and he did not turn to the right or to the left as he followed him.
Abner looked back and said, "Is that you, Asahel?" He answered, "Yes, it is."
Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right or your left. Catch one of the young men and take his armour for yourself." But Asahel would not stop chasing him.
Abner said again to Asahel, "Stop following me. Why should I have to strike you down? How could I then face your brother Joab?"

But Asahel would not turn away. So Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear, and the spear came out of his back. He fell down and died right there. Everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stopped and stood still.
But Joab and Abishai chased Abner. As the sun went down, they came to the hill of Ammah, near Giah, on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.
The men of Benjamin gathered behind Abner and formed one group, and they stood on the top of a hill.
Then Abner called out to Joab, "Must the sword keep on killing forever? Don't you know this will end in bitterness? How long before you tell your men to stop chasing their own brothers?"
Joab said, "As surely as God lives, if you had not spoken, my men would have kept chasing their brothers until morning."
So Joab blew the trumpet, and all his men stopped. They did not chase Israel any more, and they stopped fighting.
Abner and his men marched all that night through the Arabah valley. They crossed the Jordan, went through the whole region of Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
Joab came back from chasing Abner and gathered all his men. Nineteen of David's men were missing, as well as Asahel.
But David's servants had killed three hundred and sixty of Abner's men from Benjamin.
They took Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron as day was breaking.
